compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc Pro B70 (Xe-HPG-like). Triton XPU backend supports tl.dot for fp16 matmul. SIMD16/32 EU. Prefer block sizes multiple of 16. Small N=16 window means attention is essentially elementwise+tiny matmul; MLP dominates compute.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Two regimes: (1) small-N window attention per token-group (16x16) — best fused into one kernel; (2) MLP fc1 (32->128) and fc2 (128->32) — pointwise-large GEMM with C=32 and hidden=128 over N_tokens = 1*720*1280 = 921600. Both fc1/fc2 have small inner dims; can be done as fused per-row kernels.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: tl.dot may require min K=16; need to ensure fp16 accumulation path correctness.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input tensor is 1x720x1280x32 fp16 = ~58MB. Total residual+norm+MLP+attn touches multiple passes. Bandwidth-bound overall; fusion of LN+QKV+attn+proj+residual and LN+fc1+gelu+fc2+residual is the main lever.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Reloading weights per block is small (32x96, 32x32, 32x128, 128x32) — fits in cache/registers.

register_pressure.notes: Window = 16 tokens x 32 channels. Holding Q,K,V (16x32 each) plus attn (16x16) is small. MLP hidden 128 per row also fits. Per-program tile should be one window or one row to stay light.
register_pressure.risk: If we tile multiple windows per program, register pressure can climb.

nodes.notes: 1) Classification: fused transformer block = LayerNorm + window-MSA (single head, N=16, C=32, no shift, with rel-pos bias) + residual + LayerNorm + MLP (32->128->32, GELU) + residual. Dense, no indirect indexing. Reductions: LN mean/var (over C=32), softmax (over N=16). 2) Canonical: per window of 16 tokens, q,k,v=Linear(LN(x)); attn=softmax(q@k^T/sqrt(C)+rpe); out=attn@v; proj; +res. Then per token: LN; fc1; GELU; fc2; +res. 3) Layout: input (B,H,W,C)=(1,720,1280,32) fp16 contiguous, last dim C=32. Windows are 4x4 spatial groups (Wh=Ww=4), nH=180, nW=320, total windows=57600. Each window has N=16 tokens. RPE is (1,1,16,16) fp32 — cast to fp16. Weights small: qkv (96,32), proj (32,32), fc1 (128,32), fc2 (32,128). 4) Regimes: (a) Attn-fused: bandwidth-bound on x reads; tiny matmul; one program per window keeps reuse in registers. (b) MLP-fused: bandwidth-bound on x; per-row program loads 32 inputs, computes 128 hidden, then 32 output. (c) End-to-end big-fused: high register pressure, harder. 5) Knobs: program-per-window vs per-row, BLOCK_N (window count) per program, tl.dot vs manual sum, fp32 vs fp16 accum, vector width on C=32, separate vs fused LN, fused residual, RPE cast at compile-time vs load. 6) Skeleton: Kernel A (attn block): grid=(num_windows,), load 16x32 x; LN per token; matmul x@Wqkv^T to get 16x96; split; scaled q@k^T (16x16); +rpe; softmax; @v; @Wproj^T; +residual store. Kernel B (MLP): grid=(num_tokens/BLOCK_M,), load BLOCK_M x 32; LN; @W1^T+b1 -> BLOCK_M x 128; GELU; @W2^T+b2 -> BLOCK_M x 32; +residual; store. 7) Families: F1 = two-kernel fused (attn-window kernel + mlp-row kernel) — best balance; F2 = single mega-kernel fusing both — too much register pressure for window reshape; F3 = use torch matmuls for GEMM and triton only for LN/softmax/residual — simpler but loses fusion.

action.description: Implement a Triton kernel that processes one 4x4 window (16 tokens, C=32) per program: fused LayerNorm(norm1) over each of the 16 rows, compute QKV via tl.dot with packed Wqkv (96x32), compute attn scores 16x16 with scale + rpe bias, softmax, multiply by V, apply proj linear, add residual from the original x, and store back into the same (B,H,W,C) layout. Use fp32 accumulators for LN/softmax/dot. Window indexing computed from program_id mapped to (nh, nw).
action.rationale: Eliminates multiple intermediate tensors (qkv reshape/permute, attn matmuls separately) and stays bandwidth-friendly because each window only loads/stores 16*32 fp16 elements once.
action.title: Fused window-attention kernel (LN+QKV+Attn+Proj+Residual)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Need careful softmax numerical stability in fp16 (use fp32 max/sum).

action.description: Implement a Triton kernel that processes a tile of BLOCK_M tokens (each with C=32) per program: fused LayerNorm(norm2), compute hidden=GELU(x@W1^T+b1) (32->128) in registers, then out=hidden@W2^T+b2 (128->32), add residual, store back. Weights W1 (128x32) and W2 (32x128) are reloaded but small enough to be cached. Use tl.dot with fp32 accumulation.
action.rationale: Removes 3 separate kernel launches (LN, fc1+GELU, fc2+residual) and avoids materializing hidden (128-wide) in global memory, which is the largest intermediate.
action.title: Fused MLP kernel (LN+fc1+GELU+fc2+Residual)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: BLOCK_M likely 32 or 64. tl.dot shapes (BLOCK_M,32)x(32,128) and (BLOCK_M,128)x(128,32) both valid.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Two small GEMMs per tile, fully fused.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: GELU accuracy in fp16 — use tanh approximation in fp32.

action.description: First-pass implementation that keeps PyTorch matmuls for qkv/proj/fc1/fc2 but replaces LayerNorms, softmax+rpe add, GELU, and residual adds with fused Triton elementwise/reduction kernels. Used as a correctness baseline and a measurement reference for the bigger fused kernels.
action.rationale: Low risk; quickly establishes a working ModelNew that uses Triton on the primary code path while we prepare larger fused kernels.
action.title: Hybrid baseline: Triton-fused LN/softmax/GELU + torch matmuls

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin transformer block in fp16 on (1,720,1280,32) input with 4x4 windows, single head, no shift, MLP ratio 4 (hidden=128). Computation is two fused subgraphs: (A) LN -> QKV linear -> scaled q@k^T + rel-pos bias -> softmax -> @v -> proj linear -> residual; (B) LN -> fc1 -> GELU -> fc2 -> residual. All inner dims are small (C=32, N=16, hidden=128), making the workload bandwidth-bound with very many independent tiles (57600 windows / 921600 tokens). Key constraints: fp16 storage with fp32 accumulation for LN/softmax/GELU/matmul; rel-pos bias is a constant (1,1,16,16) added pre-softmax; weights are tiny and reusable across all tiles (good for cache). Best strategy is two fused Triton kernels (one per subgraph) launched per window and per token-tile, eliminating the large hidden (128-wide) and qkv (96-wide) intermediates.
open_questions: Does the Triton XPU backend's tl.dot support fp16 inputs with fp32 accumulator at small shapes like (16,32)x(32,16)?
What BLOCK_M for the MLP kernel keeps the BLOCK_M x 128 fp32 hidden tile in registers without spilling on Arc Pro B70?
Is it faster to launch one program per 4x4 window or to batch multiple windows per program to amortize weight loads?
Should weights (Wqkv, Wproj, W1, W2) be pre-transposed to make the inner-K axis contiguous for tl.dot?
How accurate must GELU be — can we use the tanh approximation, or do we need erf?
Are LayerNorm epsilon and accumulation order matched closely enough to PyTorch's fp16 LN to stay within tolerance?
Can rpe_bias be promoted to a compile-time constant via tl.constexpr or must it be loaded each program?
What is the actual cache hierarchy / SLM availability on Arc Pro B70 via Triton, and does staging weights into shared memory help?
